vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: lobstercash
Version: 0.0.11

The lobstercash skill bundle provides a comprehensive interface for AI agents to manage blockchain wallets, virtual cards, and browser-automated checkouts using the @crossmint/lobster-cli. While the skill handles sensitive financial operations and provides remote browser control, the instructions in SKILL.md and the reference files (e.g., browser.md, cards.md) consistently mandate human-in-the-loop (HITL) approvals for all transactions and emphasize transparency through live-view URLs and screenshots. The architecture specifically prevents sensitive card credentials from reaching the agent by handling them server-side during browser automation, and no indicators of malicious intent or data exfiltration were found.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement the advertised payment and checkout capabilities, but there are several internal inconsistencies and a few supply-chain/operational risks (npm global install, external update URL, conflicting CLI flag guidance) that you should review before installing or using it.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match what the instructions do: provide a CLI to manage wallets, virtual cards, browser checkout automation, x402 payments, and on-chain transactions. However, the skill metadata claims 'Required binaries: none' while the SKILL.md assumes a 'lobstercash' CLI is installed (it instructs 'npm install -g @crossmint/lobster-cli'). That gap is an inconsistency: the skill needs an external binary (npm package) even though the registry metadata doesn't declare one.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are detailed and generally scoped to payment tasks, with clear human-approval gates. Still, there are problematic or inconsistent instructions: (1) a repeated automatic 'version check on every API call' and a requirement to 'update from https://www.lobster.cash/install' if an update is required—this points to a supply-chain step that could cause users/agents to fetch code from the web; (2) internal inconsistency about the cards '--period' flag (some parts say optional, others say required), which could lead to incorrect CLI usage; (3) guidance to 'register on Base silently' (do not ask which chain) may be surprising and should be an explicit user decision in many contexts. Overall, the instructions stay within the payment/checkout domain, but the noted ambiguity and the external update requirement expand the risk surface.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the registry, but SKILL.md tells users to run 'npm install -g @crossmint/lobster-cli'. Installing a scoped npm package is common but has moderate supply-chain risk compared with an instruction-only skill: you should verify the package owner, package content, and npm publisher integrity before running a global install. The skill also instructs using an external installer page for required updates (https://www.lobster.cash/install), which increases risk if you follow it without verification.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no credentials in metadata, and the instructions emphasize human approval and server-side handling of card credentials. There are no declared secrets or unrelated environment accesses. This is proportionate for a payment/checkout tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled (always:false) and allows normal autonomous invocation (default). It does not request persistent elevation or modify other skills' configs. No concerning persistence behavior is present in the provided files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill implements an agent-driven payment/checkout CLI and largely behaves like it says, but before installing or enabling it you should: (1) verify the npm package '@crossmint/lobster-cli' on the official npm registry and confirm the publisher and package contents; (2) avoid blindly following an 'update' link—inspect what the installer would do and prefer installing from the verified npm package or official GitHub release; (3) ask the skill author (or check docs) to clarify the inconsistent guidance around the virtual card '--period' flag and the chain default behavior (automatic Base registration); (4) be aware that card credentials can be revealed by the service (sensitive data) — only proceed if you trust the lobster.cash/Crossmint service and are comfortable with approval flows that open external URLs; and (5) consider asking for a package integrity/hash or repository link before doing a global npm install. If you want, I can look up the npm package ownership and latest published version for you (if you allow me to fetch it).
